need: Frontend design, implementation, and UI audit must evaluate composition in the fixed order AI-first, Rules-first, then Grammar-last. AI-first establishes business-visible meaning, information priority, and whether dense evidence needs synthesis; Rules-first establishes hierarchy, surface ownership, nesting, responsive behavior, and semantic data presentation; Grammar-last maps that approved structure to exact components, tokens, spacing, padding, and typography. Grammar conformance alone must never make a semantically weak or visually incoherent UI pass.
negativeBoundary: Do not require AI-generated content for simple data, turn AI-first into decorative summaries, let Grammar choose product hierarchy, encode one Profile screenshot as a universal layout, or accept arbitrary visual redesign outside an approved journey and surface boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: Frontend UI direction, detail, implementation, visual-fidelity, and UI-audit contracts preserve the evaluation order AI-first, Rules-first, Grammar-last and issue an independent verdict for each layer.

AI-first requires explicit information priority and invokes synthesis only when data density or decision complexity materially benefits the user; simple label-content and short-list data remain direct.

Rules-first rejects contradictory metrics, redundant emphasis, weak hierarchy, ambiguous progress encoding, incorrect surface ownership, and responsive compositions that stop making sense before any Grammar mapping is accepted.

Grammar-last binds approved label-content structures to SurfaceCard, approved lists to SurfaceListCard, and surface-in-surface lists to the nested variant while enforcing the declared padding, gap rhythm, and type hierarchy.

Executable regression coverage proves that a Profile composition with an oversized readiness block, flat dense identity data, misleading skill progress bars, or Grammar-correct but semantically incoherent nesting cannot receive a passing UI verdict.
Product implementation can consume the resolved learning without copying the Profile example as a fixed page template or widening to unrelated Dashboard and navigation surfaces.

accepts: Use AI-first to decide content priority and synthesis need before choosing surfaces or visual treatments.
Use Rules-first to validate hierarchy, meaning, surface ownership, nesting, and responsive coherence.
Use Grammar-last to bind the approved composition to SurfaceCard, nested SurfaceListCard, spacing, padding, and typography contracts.
Treat the approved Profile visualization as bounded evidence of the reasoning order, not as a universal template.
rejects: Pass a UI because Grammar components and class names are technically valid while the information architecture remains weak.
Place a large readiness surface above stronger identity and learning evidence merely because the block already exists.
Represent categorical skill counts as progress bars or present top 0 percent as a meaningful positive summary.
Apply uniform gaps and font sizes without considering semantic hierarchy, content density, and neighboring element scale.

review.rationale: The visible Profile evidence and approved three-layer visualization prove a reusable failure mode: semantic priority and surface logic must be validated before Grammar mapping. Resolve the learning urgently while preserving the bounded negative rules against forced AI content, Profile-template overfitting, and unrelated surface redesign.
